problem:
The charge $q(t)$ on the capacitor, in coulombs, in a series RCL circuit at time $t$ seconds is

$$
q(t)=4{e}^{-2t}-{e}^{-6t}+\frac{12}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\frac{5}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t).
$$

Find, in amperes, the exact amplitude of the steady-state **current** $I$ in this circuit.

The amplitude of the steady-state current is
{{field-1}}
amperes.
worked_solution:
The current $I$ measured in amperes, is defined as the rate of flow of charge $q$ measured in coulombs.

$$
I=\frac{dq}{dt}
$$

Differentiating the given expression for $q(t),$ we obtain the following expression for $I,$ in amperes:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(t) & =\frac{d}{dt}(4{e}^{-2t}-{e}^{-6t}+\frac{12}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)-\frac{5}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)) \\  & =-8{e}^{-2t}+6{e}^{-6t}-\frac{60}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)-\frac{25}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t).\end{aligned}
$$

Note the following:

- The quantity ${I}_{c}(t)=-8{e}^{-2t}+6{e}^{-6t}$ is the *transient current*, since it goes to zero as $t\to \infty .$

- The function ${I}_{p}(t)=-\frac{60}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)-\frac{25}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)$ is the *steady-state current*. It governs the current's long-term behavior.

Therefore, as $t\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
I(t)≈{I}_{p}(t)=-\frac{60}{17}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)-\frac{25}{17}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t).
$$

Finally, the amplitude of the steady-state current, in amperes, is given by

$$
\sqrt{{(-\frac{60}{17})}^{2}+{(-\frac{25}{17})}^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{4225}{289}}=\frac{65}{17}.
$$
